BEHAVIOURAL OBJECTIVES: Students should be able to: 1. Define science and technology. 2. Describe the concept society. 3. Highlight the importance of science and technology. Definition of science and technology. The word science comes from the latin word “sciens” which means “to know”. Science is an organised body of knowledge that has been observed, tested and supported with facts. Science can be viewed as a way of gathering and organizing information about the natural world. Science begins with curiosity. Man’s desire to understand the environment in which he lives, holds the key to all his knowledge of the world. Man is by nature basically curious and wants to know the ‘why’ and ‘how’ of things. He wants to know what makes them and why they act the way they do. Science is the order of systematic investigation of such questions. Scientist learn through reading, thinking, experimenting and by sharing ideas with each other. Science does not only deal with concrete phenomena, which can be readily observed; it also deals with ideas in the mind [that is with the abstract]. Science follows a logical pattern observing natural phenomena. Therefore, science may be defined as a process by which new knowledge and understanding of the world is acquired. The scientific pattern in solving problems are: Recognise the problem, State an explanation [hypothesis], Collect data, Test the hypothesis and draw the conclusion. Technology is described as the application of a scientific knowledge to solve practical problems. There are many problems in our society today which are solved through the application of scientific knowledge. Science and technology work hand in hand. They are closely and intimately related. Society is an organised group of people living together in a particular area. A society is made up of people who live closely and interact together. Society embraces human beings, their activities in relation to their natural and social environment. Each of the societies has specific references to their physical environment, occupy a specific area, and share a common language and common way of life. Importance of Science and Technology Science and Technology have helped us in many areas of human activities such as health, education, social life, transportation, communication, agriculture, government etc. ❖ Science and technology has made possible polio vaccine to reduce child mortality. It has brought about weather satellites which we use to forecast the weather condition and prevent untimely death by aircraft. ❖ Science and technology has introduce the use of computer gadgets which makes teaching, researching and learning more simple and easy to explore.

❖ It brought about electronic gadgets which makes mass media closer to the people through information. ❖ The water we use has been scientifically treated and purified for consumption. ❖ The use of electric light and comfort of a heated or air conditioned home is made available through science and technology. ❖ Through science and technology there is widespread use of machinery in agriculture as well as the application of scientific advances and discoveries. ❖ Better clothing is available because science and technology have provided better fabrics and improved methods of textile manufacture. ❖ Scientific technology has also made possible the development of better soaps, shoes, furniture, more nourishing food for our bodies, better materials for building homes and more effective drugs to cure or prevent diseases to help people live longer and healthier. ❖ Science and technology have contributed to the development of agriculture with sophisticated farm equipment to make farm work easier and faster. ❖ Science and technology has help in creating more jobs and in the manufacturing of goods and services. ❖ It has assisted in improving the standard of living among the people. ❖ It has provided a sound knowledge of organizing and managing both human and natural resources. Identify five importance of science and technology. 4. Describe Society WEEK 2: SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY & THE SOCIETY II BEHAVIOURAL OBJECTIVES: Students should be able to: 1. State the traditional science and technology. 2. Mention some traditional science and technologies influenced by modernisation. Traditional science and technology. Before the arrival of Europeans in Nigeria, science and technology existed but they were not recognised as such. They were regarded as magic, which had no clear explanations, so

were seen as sacred. Man in primitive society learnt some aspect of science, which later formed the basis for modern science. In olden days, man learnt to identify food plants and how to cultivate them. He learnt how to identify medicinal herbs. The steps involved in determining these food plants and medicinal herbs must have come through scientific experimentation. Man’s ability to make pottery works like clay pots used in cooking or for preserving water shows that science and technology existed in traditional Nigerian society before the introduction of modern science. Moreover, man’s ability to make implements like hoes, machetes, hooks, bows and arrows, axes and weapons that were needed to solve his environmental problems such as farming and hunting shows that the early or ancient man had the knowledge of science and technology. In the olden day’s Nigerian communities had traditional healers who served the roles of doctors. They were experts in treating different ailments, especially local treatment of wounds and fractures of bones. We also had traditional midwife who helped women give birth safely. The making of canoes, and casting of brass and bronze objects by different ethnic groups in Nigeria, were all indications that science and technology had already been in practice before the arrival of the Europeans to Nigeria. The preservation of food by salting and drying it in the sun were all practice of traditional science. Local soaps were made from ash for bathing and messages were sent out through town crier, who used metal or wooden gongs to pass information or use of smoke. Traditional science and technology influenced by modernization. 1. The introduction of modern science and technology such as tractors, computers, mobile phones and calculators has made work easier and faster and less mistakes in their work. 2. The use of electric fans, air conditioners, electric cooker, electric kettle, juice extractor, blender electronics and other devices make man’s life more comfortable and interesting. 3. Science and technology create job opportunities.

4. Science and technology have introduced mechanised farming, the use of modern machines that make mass production of food possible with the use of fertilizers to improve agricultural output. 5. They have helped in improving the quality of education in many societies. 6. Nowadays through science and technology, a child can be conceived, doctors are perfecting ways of replacing a faulty heart, and other organs of the body with healthy ones through the transplant system. 7. Modern roads, bridges, motorcars, aeroplanes, modern trains, ship e.t.c. are some of the familiar products of modern science and technology. Exercises: a. Describe Traditional science and technology. b. Mention some traditional science and technology influence by modernisation... Outline the causes of breakdown of home appliance. 2. State the correct ways of using electrical appliances. Causes of breakdown of home appliances.

• Lack of maintaining culture of our home appliances can cause breakdown. • Careless keeping of most of the appliances. • Not been careful of the power we use on the appliances as long as it is working. • Buying of sub – standard product all in the name that the product is cheap. • Just allowing any person to help in solving any challenge without consulting expert. • Allowing many hands to operate the appliance can cause the breakdown. • Allowing water to pour on home appliance can weaken the capacity to function properly. • Exposure of naked wire of appliances can reduce power voltage in them. • Unconducive environment for using appliances • The correct ways of using electrical appliances. • • The most proper way of using electrical appliances is to read and study the instruction properly before attempting it. • • Another proper way of using electrical appliance is to allow the expert of that product to teach you. • • It is also important to know the current voltage required for every electrical appliance. • • Avoid the contact of water or liquid product from getting in contact with electrical appliances because it can shock the person that want to use it. • • Switch off all electrical appliances after use immediately or when there is interruption in power. • • Fire extinguisher should be installed at specified place in the house where every body can easily assess it. WEEK 6&7 NATIONAL ECONOMY I & 2 “SAVING AND WAYS OF SAVING” BEHAVIOURAL OBJECTIVES: Students should be able to: 1. Define Saving. 2. Mention various ways of saving in the past. 3. Enumerate modern ways of saving. 4. State the need for keeping money in the bank 5. List the advantages of keeping money in the bank 6. Outline the problems people are facing in keeping money in the bank. Definition of Saving. Saving can be defined as a method of keeping money and other valuables such as certificate, will, jewellery, land survey and so on in a safe place which could either be in the bank or a hidden safe box in the house. Ways of Saving in the past. 1. You can save money or valuables by rapping it with cloth or paper and digging a pit in the compound to keep till when needed. 2. You can save by giving money to someone trusted who comes to collect it on daily bases or weekly bases till when you are in need of the money or valuables. 3. You can save money saving box where by you can only have easy way of dropping the money but will have to break or destroy the box before you can collect the money. 4. You can also save by joining a group of people who will be contributing together and each person will have a particular date to collect whatever you have contributed. 5. You can also save when you join a group contributing the same amount and each person will be giving everybody money at a particular time. 6. You can save in an empty clay pot buried in the ground at home or on the farm for future needs. 7. You can keep your money under the pillow. Modern ways of saving. 1. You can save in the bank either savings or current account which can be withdraw anytime. 2. You can save in the bank for fixed deposit which will require a period of specified time as agreement before you can withdraw 3. You can save by buying treasure bills from government can later increase in value and converted back to money. 4. You can keep valuables in the bank for future needs and prevention from been stolen or destroy by natural or man-made disaster.

5. You can also save for future of your children or your old age by investing in buying shares which could later in the future sold to generate more. 6. You can save with the cooperative societies who helps you to acquire properties. The need for saving. 1. The major reason for saving is to prepare for the future well-being of yourself and family at large. 2. Another reason for saving is to prevent wasteful spending on irrelevant things or what is not needed urgently. 3. The need to save is to prevent it from been stolen at home. 4. It also makes you to be prudent in your spending. Advantages of keeping money in the bank. 1. It makes you to plan your expenses properly. 2. The money is safe. 3. It prevents you from unwanted buying. The problems people encounter during banking. 1. It consumes much time any time you need to save in the bank. 2. It requires little education to know how to read and write when banking 3. You can face mis – manage of your money if not properly monitored especially those bankers in charge of your fixed deposit. 4. There could be the problem of irregular signature of the owner of the account due to long time of signing in the bank. 5. The bank can over charge the bank dues which will reduce the money budgeted for that time. 6. The bank can debit you on the use of A.T.M. which use to take some time before it is reverse. Exercises: 1. What is banking? 2. Highlight five ways of banking in the past. 3. State four modern ways of banking. 4. Mention three advantages of banking. 5. State five problems people encounter during banking 6. State the advantages of keeping money in the bank WEEK 8: NATIONAL ECONOMY “COMMUNICATION” BEHAVIOURAL OBJECTIVES: Students should be able to: 1. Define communication.

2. Mention the traditional and modern means of communication. 3. Enumerate the roles of communication in national economy. Definition of communication Communication can be described as the means of passing information or messages from a sender through a medium to a receiver. Communication involves sending and receiving messages. Means of communication. Communication can take different forms or means which includes communicating by writing, verbal means, physical actions or signals. Messages can be sent to a very close or very far place or anywhere across the globe. Traditional means of communication. Communication in the olden days varies as the environment where the message is going will detain the means by which the sender will use for easy interpretation and understanding. Traditional communication involves the use of local means to pass across information or messages from location to other or from one person to another. The following are traditional means of communication the use of fire, smokes, signals such as leaves, mirror, drums, gongs, cannon shots, bells, flutes, whistles, horns, letter writing and even human beings as town crier e.t.c. Modern means of communication. Communication by modern means is the dissemination of information to many people in many places at the same time with the help of modern machines such as the television, radio, print media as in newspapers, magazine, postal system using for mailing, telegram, telex, fax, social networks as in email, twitter, histogram, whatsup, mobile phoning, Facebook, e.t.c. Roles of communication in national economy. 1. Communication has made it possible to send vital information across the globe in a quick, easy and fast means. It has turned the whole world into a global village. 2. Communication make transportation possible e.g. radio puts captian in touch with the shore. Also pilot gets in touch with the control tower through radio. 3. Transport and communication are so important to the national economy well-being of the country as they facilitate movement of people and interaction. 4. Communication is advancing rapidly which brings interaction between nations of the world regardless of race or colour.

5. Communication has help the under develop country by helping them to refine their available resources which has promote their standard of living. 6. Communication has help to reduce child mortality rate to the minimal as a result of enlightening the public on free health care services. 7. Communication has promoted trade among costal line nations which are source of income for the country. 8. Communication facilitates have helped to save a lot of lives because people can call for help in cases of emergency. 9. Communication promotes business i. e. it enables manufacturer, wholesaler, and retailer to remain in constant touch with one another, thereby promoting easy flow of goods and services from manufacturers to consumers. 10. Communication helps to bridge the gap between the leader and the followers, thereby promoting cordial relationship and reducing suspicion, hatred and sabotage. Exercises: 1. What do you understand by the term communication? 2. Mention some means of communicating. 3. Define traditional means of communication. 4. Enumerate some modern means of communication. 5. Highlight four roles of communication in national economy. WEEK 9: FINDING HELP BEHAVIOURAL OBJECTIVES: Students should be able to: 1. State the meaning of finding help. 2. Mention the situation when people need help. 3. Enumerate people who can help. 4. Highlight the skills necessary when seeking help. 5. Identify the skills necessary for helping others. 6. List the importance of finding help. Meaning of finding help. Finding help involves providing or seeking assistance or support in order to find a remedy or relief from a problem or make a situation more bearable. Help is the act of assisting people who are in need, trouble, pain, distressed, or victimized. Situations when people need help.

There are many times when young people may need help though they may not always ask for help. However, the following situations may present a problem that may require help: 1. Relationships – emotional, upheavals, concerns about changes in the body, poverty, lack of shelter, harassment or bullying, educationally related problems, loss of personal items, unplanned pregnancy, drug/alcohol dependency, confusion resulting from conflicting messages e.g. societal and family values, divorce or separation of parents, household disaster e.g. fire, flood, loss of home, violence, bereavement and financial problems. 2. People who can help or sources of help. a. Parents/guardians and other family members b. Counsellors e.g. school’s counsellors c. Religious leaders. d. Health practitioners. e. Teachers. f. Specialised institutions. g. Trusted experienced adults. h. Law enforcement agents. i. Social workers. j. Adolescent focused NGOs. k. Community members. l. Security personnel. Skills necessary when seeking help. a. Good communication skills: ability to explain the problem or the need. b. Assertiveness: willingness to speak up, explain the issue. c. Counselling: willingness to learn or seek advice from a professional on the problem through discussion. d. Follow – up: ability to take action on what to be done to rectify the situation. e. Politeness: you must not ask for help using a commanding tone. Always remember to use the word “please” when asking for help. f. Being Observant: you should be able to tell dubious people from those who can genuinely help you. g. Listening skill: they are vital for interpersonal communication. When the other person has finished talking, you may need to ask questions to ensure you have received their message; help the speaker to feel free to speak. Skills necessary when helping others.

1. Ensuring a conducive atmosphere [friendliness, sense of security that what is being said will be held in confidence, privacy from being overheard]. 2. Good listening technique [hearing and checking out with the person to ensure that you understand what he/she has said. 3. Empathy [the ability to imagine and share another person’s feelings, experience, problems etc. 4. Counselling [ability to refer the case or the problem to a professional 5. Follow – up [taking to help in whatever you can]. Steps to take when help is needed. a. Identify the concern. b. Recognise that help is needed. c. Keep calm, stay focused and try not to be nervous. d. Look for a trusted adult [ i.e. a parent, teacher, guardian, health care worker, religious leader, agency counsellor] and inform him/her. e. Wait for assistance to be provided, follow the directions of those providing assistance. f. Try to inform your parent/guardian, if possible, state the situation. g. If possible, seek help in company of trusted and supportive friends. Hindrances to finding help for young people. 1. Ignorance [that help is even available, or that the situation can even be rectified. 2. Non – conducive environment. 3. Lack of adequate knowledge about available services [many people are unaware that there is any help available; they may be aware of an agency but not know how it can be of help]. 4. Inaccessibility of services [distance to be travelled, cost of services, restrictions on use, all make a service inaccessible. 5. Fear of adults – some young people may out of fear find it difficult to approach adults because adults can be abusive or unapproachable. Importance of finding help. a. It makes it easier for one to cope with problem/concerns. b. It gives solutions to problems/concerns. c. It gives an idea of where to go for additional help when it needed. d. It relieves emotional trauma.

e. It can improve. Exercises: 1. What does it mean to find help? 2. What problems/situations may require help? 3. Mention sources of help. 4. What skills are necessary when finding help? 5. State five steps that should be taken when help is need. 6. Explain four importance of finding help. 7. Identify four characteristics of agencies that provide help 8. State five hindrances to finding for young people
